correctness.rationale: The integral symmetric-power substitution B_d of Fibonacci matrix A has B_d^5≡I (mod 5) for all d divisible by 4. Lifting gives B_d^(5^(r−1))=I+5^(r−1)D and ∑_{j=0}^4B_d^(j·5^(r−1))≡5I (mod 5^r), proving S_r(n)≡5S_(r−1)(n) (mod 5^r). The Fibonacci indicator pattern gives S_1(n)≡−1 mod 5. Induction yields uniform S_r(n)≡−5^(r−1) mod 5^r. Every window of length 5^r u has valuation exactly r−1; when 5∤k the first two windows differ by F_k^d≡1 mod5. The executable performed 600 block tests and 1120 exact GCD tests. Quantifiers include all n,k and all positive d divisible by four; finite checks are corroborative.

originality.rationale: Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches identified the closest published quartic local theorem, whose explicitly excluded small primes include five. A second odd-quartic theorem excludes lengths divisible by five, so it cannot cover the first nontrivial five-primary case k=25. Mbirika–Spilker studies squares and asks about higher powers; Adegoke studies exact individual sums, not translated-window gcds. Direct full-text implication comparisons do not cover the stated all-fourth-multiple exponent law. Absence of an indexed equivalent is not treated as a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently formulated recurrence-theoretic congruence theorem could imply this result.
Classical individual quartic-sum identities might permit a further derivation not identified in the inspected work; this is a bibliographic rather than a proof gap.

value.rationale: The prime-five factor of the full quartic window GCD is an explicit missing case of a published prime-by-prime classification. Its valuation is ν5(k)−1 for 25|k rather than full ν5(k), with no factor until k=25; this explains a ramified-prime cancellation phenomenon. A uniform congruence proves all translates have the same sharp valuation and extends the mechanism to every exponent divisible by four, giving a motivated structural family rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
